7805.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : BM6638 : OMICS in Biotechnology { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module 1: Introduction to Omics Technologies
Overview and general principles of omics technologies in biotechnology, Omics approaches: Genomics, Proteomics, Transcriptomics and Metabolomics, Meta-omics (genomics, proteomics, transcriptomics, metabolomics) and Functional omics
Module 2: Applications of Omics in Biotechnology
Application of Omics in different fields of biotechnology including agriculture, environment, pharmaceuticals, medicine, forensic, discovery of novel organisms, enzymes, value added products etc.,
Module 3: Genomics and Genomic Technologies
Genomics, covering DNA sequencing technologies (e.g., DNA-sequencing, Genome Sequencing, Next Generation Sequencing (NGS), gene expression microarray), genome annotation, and computational tools for data analysis.
Module 4: Proteomics, Transcriptomics and Metabolomics
Tools for Proteomics techniques like mass spectrometry, protein separation methods (e.g., SDS-PAGE, 2D-PAGE). The Transcriptomics techniques including RNA-Seq, gene expression microarrays, and the role of regulatory RNAs like miRNAs and lncRNAs. The Metabolomics techniques covers NMR, mass spectrometry, and GC.
Module 5: Meta-Omics and Functional Omics
Basics of Meta-Omics, which integrates multiple Omics data for a holistic understanding of biological systems, and Functional Omics, which helps discover novel organisms, enzymes, and bio-products.
Module 7: Computational Tools for Omics Data Analysis
Computational Tools for Omics data analysis, including bioinformatics platforms, data integration techniques, and machine learning for predictive modeling. Designing of Omics-based research, covering data collection, analysis, and ethical considerations.

Course Objective

1 .

1. To understand the general principles and methodologies of omics technologies (genomics, proteomics, transcriptomics, and metabolomics).
2 .

2. To gain knowledge about the applications of omics in biotechnology across various sectors (agriculture, environment, pharmaceuticals, medicine, forensics).
3 .

3. To analyze omics data through computational approaches, including data integration, big data handling, and genome annotation.
4 .

4. To understand the significance of meta-omics and functional omics in the discovery of novel organisms, enzymes, and value-added products for biotechnology-driven industries.

Course Outcome

1 .

Upon completion of this course, students will be able to:
1. Explain the principles and strategies behind genomics, proteomics, transcriptomics, and metabolomics technologies.
2. Demonstrate the ability to conduct basic experiments using various omics tools (e.g., DNA sequencing, RNA-Seq, Mass Spectrometry).
3. Integrate various omics data (genomics, proteomics, transcriptomics, metabolomics) to make biological discoveries and predictions.
4. Apply omics technologies to solve real-world problems in biotechnology sectors like agriculture, pharmaceuticals, medicine, and forensics.
5. Design omics-based research projects to discover novel organisms, enzymes, and valuable bio-products.

Essential Reading

1 .

DebmalyaBarh Vasco Azevedo, Omics Technologies and Bio-engineering, 1st Edition, Volume 1: Towards Improving Quality of Life, Academic Press

2 .

Wittmann, C. and Lee, S.Y. eds, Systems metabolic engineering, Springer Science & Business Media

Module 1 :

Module 1 (8 hours) :

Lithography, Oxidation, Ion implantation, Metalization, and Diffusion techniques. BASIC ELECTRICAL PROPERTIES OF MOS, CMOS & BICOMS CIRCUITS: Ids-Vds relationships, Threshold voltage Vt, Gm, Gds and Wo, Pass Transistor, MOS, CMOS & Bi CMOS Inverters, Zpu/Zpd, MOS Transistor circuit model, Latch-up in CMOS circuits.

COMBINATIONAL LOGIC NETWORKS: Layouts, Simulation, Network delay, interconnect design, power optimization, Switch logic networks, Gate and Network testing.
Module 4 (6 Hours)
SEQUENTIAL SYSTEMS: Memory cells and Arrays, clocking disciplines, System Design, power optimization, Design validation, and testing.
Module 5 (6 Hours)
FLOOR PLANNING & ARCHITECTURE DESIGN: Floor planning methods, off-chip connections, High-level synthesis, Architecture for low power, SOCs and Embedded CPUs, and Architecture testing.

INTRODUCTION TO CAD SYSTEMS (ALGORITHMS) AND CHIP DESIGN: Layout Synthesis and Analysis, Scheduling and printing, Hardware/Software Co-design, chip design methodologies- A simple Design example.

It offers a profound understanding of the design of complex digital VLSI circuits, computeraided simulation and synthesis tool for hardware design

To bring both Circuits and System views on design together

To provide knowledge in ASIC design and implementation.

1 .

and beliefs in shaping vernacular architecture – the spirit of a place.
Module II (9 hours)
Rural shelter and settlements:
Characteristics of rural shelter and settlements in global perspectives, such as nomadic-semi-nomadic living in extreme climates, moorland and farmsteads, hamlets, villages, and others Examples from India – Bhunga house, Khidrat and Jalwali house, Chittilu house, Meitei
Yumjao house, Chang house, Bengal house, Kath-kuni house, and others.
Assignment(s): Seminars on case studies from different regions of India.
Module III (6 hrs)
Materials and structural systems:
Various materials used Importance of physical principles in structural systems components of structural systems and their regional nomenclature Learning about the vernacular construction skills Case studies.
Module IV (6 hrs)
Dimensions of vernacular architecture:
Creating built environment, resources used, strategies to cope with climate Understanding living spaces Values, meanings, and symbols, decorative characteristics.
Assignment: debate/group discussion/essay explaining the importance of studying
vernacular architecture in today’s context.

Course Objective

1 .

To understand the basic philosophy of ‘Vernacular’ and its relevance in the present context.
2 .

To identify various factors behind the shaping of vernacular architecture.
3 .

To understand the process of development of vernacular architecture of different regions.

Course Outcome

1 .

1. An ability to understand the various dimensions of vernacular architecture.
2. An ability to acknowledge and analyse the impacts of culture, social norms and beliefs, geographic
location and other factors on vernacular architecture.
3. An ability to learn vernacular methods and techniques of building construction and to assess the potential of integrating these in architecture.
